$comment: Rules about where a figure came from, when it was true, and whether the document admits what it does not know. Standards 21, 26, and 27. One rule here — data.attestation-digests-current — is the only `structural` full-assurance rule about evidence in the framework, and its narrowness is the point: it establishes that reviewed content has not changed, and nothing whatever about the quality of the review.
$note: Standard 21 has no `calc` blocks at all, and that absence is itself a claim. Every other standard in the series that reaches full assurance reaches it about arithmetic; freshness is not a computable property, so no rule here from Standard 21 claims more than `partial`, and none is described as though it did.

rules.title: Every externally sourced figure carries an as-of date
rules.description: Each figure the document presents as coming from outside it — a price, a rate, a yield, an index level — carries the date on which it was current.
rules.rationale: A figure with no date cannot be judged stale, and staleness is the one defect in market data that grows without anyone touching the document. The date is what lets a later reader decide whether the analysis still stands, rather than assuming it does.
rules.remediation: Attach the as-of date at the point each external figure is used, not once at the top of the document where it does not reach the figure.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical: it establishes that a date is PRESENT beside the figure, never that the date is ACCURATE. A figure labelled "as of 2026-08-01" that was in fact copied out of a document written in 2023 satisfies this rule perfectly, and nothing available to this repository can contradict it. What the rule establishes is that the document has the SHAPE of an attributable document, which is a real property and a much weaker one than it looks.

rules.title: Every externally sourced figure names its source
rules.description: Each externally sourced figure names who published it, specifically enough that a reader could retrieve the same figure.
rules.rationale: An unattributed figure cannot be checked, and an unverifiable figure is indistinguishable from an invented one to every reader who does not already know the answer — which is every reader the document was written for.
rules.remediation: Name the publisher and the specific series or instrument beside the figure, with a reference or link where one exists.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical. It establishes that an attribution is PRESENT, never that the named source exists or says what is claimed. A fabricated figure with a fabricated citation passes cleanly; that is prohibited.fabricated-market-data's subject, and it is not automatable at all because establishing that a figure was not invented requires the true value.

rules.title: The document declares the freshness its conclusions require
rules.description: The document states how current its inputs must be for its conclusions to hold, and what must be re-checked once that window has passed.
rules.rationale: Different conclusions decay at different speeds: a claim resting on an annual allowance survives a year, a claim resting on a bond yield may not survive a week. Without a stated window the reader has no basis for deciding when the document stopped being true, so they assume it has not.
rules.remediation: State the freshness window for each class of input the conclusion depends on, and the condition that would require the analysis to be redone.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical: it establishes that a threshold is DECLARED, never that it is the RIGHT threshold, and never that the document's own figures satisfy it. Whether a given figure is stale for the decision it informs depends on what decision the reader faces and how fast that class of data moves, neither of which is in the document — Standard 21 keeps that question out of the catalog for exactly that reason.

rules.title: Every figure carries its origin, and the origin is one of the permitted kinds
rules.description: Monetary figures, rates, and index levels carry either a named source with an as-of date, an explicit assumption disclosure, or a Standard 27 marker naming what is missing.
rules.rationale: A figure with no declared origin invites the reader to treat it as observed, because observation is the default reading of a bare number. Requiring one of exactly three provenances makes the difference between what was looked up, what was assumed, and what is not known a property of the text rather than of the reader's charity.
rules.remediation: Attach an origin to every figure: a source with a date, an assumption with a basis, or a marker naming the missing input and the conclusion that depends on it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical, and it says so plainly: it establishes that an attribution is PRESENT beside a figure, never that the attribution is ACCURATE. A fabricated figure with a fabricated citation passes it cleanly. That is not a defect to be fixed in a later version — it is the permanent limit of reading a document without access to the world the document describes.

rules.title: Every attestation's recorded digest matches the content it attests to
rules.description: For each path an attestation names, the digest recorded when the review was made matches the digest of that content now.
rules.rationale: A human judgement is evidence about the artifact that was reviewed, not about whatever later occupies the same path. Without the digest an attestation goes on vouching for content nobody has looked at, which is the mechanism by which a piece of evidence quietly becomes a waiver.
rules.remediation: Re-review the changed content and record a new attestation with a fresh digest. Never update the digest without redoing the review — that is precisely the weakening Standard 29 forbids.
rules.$assuranceNote: FULL, and legitimately so: the question is exact and admits no judgement — the content either hashes to what was recorded or it does not, and where it does not, the rule returns to NOT_EVALUATED on its own without anyone remembering to look. What it emphatically does NOT establish is that the review was competent, thorough, or honest. No mechanism in this repository establishes any of those, and Standard 26 R3 forbids implying otherwise. Full assurance is claimed for the narrow question of content identity and for nothing else.

rules.title: A claim needing external data the document does not have carries the marker
rules.description: A claim resting on a current external figure the document does not carry — a price, a rate, a yield, an index level — carries a [requires current external data] marker inside the claim's own block.
rules.rationale: Without the marker a reader cannot distinguish an analysis conditional on a figure nobody has from one built on a figure someone looked up. The two read identically and lead to different actions, and only one of them should.
rules.remediation: Mark the claim where it appears, name the specific figure that is missing, and state the conclusion as conditional on it. A document-level disclaimer does not reach the claim and does not satisfy this.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical, and partial in two directions at once. It establishes that a marker is PRESENT within a claim's block — never that it is the RIGHT marker or that it names the right missing input — and it cannot find the gap an author never wrote about at all. A document that assumes a current rate without ever mentioning that a current rate was needed passes cleanly, and that is the standard's most serious violation. Whether the marker was placed thoughtfully or pasted onto every row is equally beyond it.

rules.title: A claim needing personal circumstances the document does not have carries the marker
rules.description: A claim resting on the reader's circumstances the document does not carry — income, tax position, horizon, obligations, holdings — carries a [requires personal financial context] marker inside the claim's own block.
rules.rationale: An unmarked gap in personal context gets filled by assumption, and a silently assumed circumstance produces an analysis of a person who does not exist, addressed to a person who does. The marker is the only signal the reader gets that the mismatch is possible.
rules.remediation: Mark the claim where it appears, name the circumstance that is missing, and present the conclusion as conditional on it rather than choosing a value for it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Lexical. It establishes that a marker is PRESENT within the claim's block — never that the marker names the right missing input, and never that the unmarked claims are complete. A silent assumption is by definition unmarked, so the checker cannot see the thing it is looking for: it can only observe that the document uses the mechanism somewhere. The placement requirement is checkable in one direction only and the checker takes that direction — a marker inside the block satisfies it, a document-level notice does not.
